edits.text: - Prefer a cut after an immediately following identifying element (a proper name, essential appositive, or numeral+unit) over a cut between the preceding noun or role noun and that element; as a last resort, take a cut between them only when the identifier is followed by punctuation or a clear clause boundary.

Keep a noun or role noun together with the immediately following identifying element that completes or disambiguates it (proper name, essential appositive, or numeral+unit) when no intervening clause boundary or punctuation separates them.

- Prefer a cut after an identifying element when that element immediately follows a common or role noun with no intervening punctuation or clause boundary. An identifying element is a proper name, an essential appositive/identifier, or a numeral plus its unit. Prefer cutting after that identifying element over a cut between the noun and it; if the identifying element exceeds four contiguous words, prefer the cut after the noun.

edits._was: - Will a cut split a coordination or contrast relation so that emphasis, contrast, or entailment between clauses is lost, reversed, or made ambiguous in the joined translation?
